solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bond is on alert breaking in!

indicators.note: the words 'is on alert' break apart and their letters are put back together in a new order

parts.note: in, meaning fashionable, is HIP

explanation.surface: A spy like James Bond is on high alert as he breaks into a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' looks like the spy, but here it means a connection; 'breaking' is the anagram signal, not a burglary.
explanation.definitionFit: A bond between people is a connection or tie, the same thing as a relationship.

clue.text: Royal Engineers gathering in memory

parts.note: RE is the abbreviation for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
a gathering of things is a collection

explanation.surface: An army corps' reunion stirs up old memories.
explanation.definitionFit: A memory of something past is a recollection; the two are direct synonyms.

clue.text: Charged a lot in Los Angeles retreat

parts.note: a den is a private retreat or hideaway

explanation.surface: Someone paid a lot at a pricey hideaway in Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charged' looks like being billed, but it means loaded, as a cart is charged with goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Laden means heavily loaded, and to charge something is an old sense of loading it.

clue.text: Whirlwind is to trouble, sucking in Royal Navy

indicators.note: the pair of words draws another piece into its middle, as a whirlwind sucks things up

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: A storm causes havoc and pulls in ships of the navy.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violent rotating column of air, a kind of whirlwind.

clue.text: Duck small victim for large bird

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nought, so O
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a victim is prey

explanation.surface: A large bird of prey swoops on a small duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' is a zero score in cricket, giving the letter O, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The osprey is a big fish-eating raptor, an example of a large bird.

clue.text: Southern wine brewed for strength

indicators.note: brewing mixes things up, so the letters of 'wine' are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A wine from the south is made to give a drinker strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinew is tendon, and figuratively means physical strength or power.

clue.text: Anger that smoulders in RC service?

definitions.meaning: to make them very angry, a verb sense
the aromatic substance burnt during Roman Catholic Mass

explanation.surface: Fury smoulders quietly during a Catholic service.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to enrage; as a noun it is fragrant resin burnt in church rituals.

clue.text: One like Noah, after flood, finding insect?

indicators.note: the boatman piece comes after the flood piece in the answer

parts.note: a flood is water
Noah, who sailed the ark, was a boatman

explanation.surface: Noah, after the great flood, finds an insect on the ark.
explanation.definitionFit: The water boatman is an aquatic bug that rows with its legs, a kind of insect.

clue.text: Regressing predictably involves this drink

indicators.note: regressing means going backwards, so the run of letters is read in reverse
the word predictably contains a run of letters within it

explanation.surface: Drinking this predictably makes people behave childishly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involves' finds REDIC inside 'predictably', and 'Regressing' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Cider is an alcoholic drink made from fermented apple juice.

clue.text: Dad swallowing an excellent remedy for ills

indicators.note: the first piece takes the others inside it, as if gulping them down

parts.note: pa is an informal word for dad
ace means excellent

explanation.surface: Father takes a superb cure-all medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: A panacea is a supposed cure for all diseases or problems, a universal remedy.

clue.text: Eagle in whirling descent

indicators.note: whirling spins the letters of 'Eagle in' round into a new order

explanation.surface: An eagle spirals as it comes down from the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'descent' suggests a bird's dive, but here it means ancestry.
explanation.definitionFit: Descent in the sense of family origin is lineage, one's line of ancestors.

clue.text: Grimace when church pursues gain

indicators.note: the church piece follows, or chases, the gain piece in the answer

parts.note: to gain is to win
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone pulls a face when the church chases profit.
explanation.definitionFit: To wince is to make a brief pained facial expression, much like a grimace.

clue.text: Xmas booze g-g-gone astray!

indicators.note: letters gone astray have wandered out of place and must be put back in a new order

explanation.surface: A stuttering drinker finds the Christmas drink has run out.
explanation.walkthrough: The stammered 'g-g-gone' supplies three Gs plus ONE, which 'astray' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggnog is a creamy drink of eggs, milk and spirits traditionally served at Christmas.

clue.text: Left in strong wind on ship

indicators.note: the letter for left goes in the middle of the wind word

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind

explanation.surface: A sailing ship is blown to port by a gale.
explanation.definitionFit: A galleon was a large multi-decked sailing vessel, a type of ship.

clue.text: Clearly providing an example of this!

definitions.text: Clearly providing an example of this!

parts.words: Clearly providing an example of this!
parts.note: the first word of the clue, 'Clearly', is itself an example of the part of speech the answer names

explanation.surface: Something is plainly shown as an illustration.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is self-referential: 'Clearly' ends in -ly and modifies a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Words like 'clearly' modify verbs or adjectives, the grammatical class this word names.

clue.text: Little animals in sleeping quarters freeze

parts.note: a dorm, short for dormitory, is a room for sleeping
to freeze is to ice

explanation.surface: Small creatures shiver in a freezing dormitory.
explanation.definitionFit: Dormice are small hibernating rodents, little animals famous for sleeping.

clue.text: Falling star, remote, exploded

indicators.note: an exploded word is blown apart, so the letters of 'remote' land in a new order

explanation.surface: A distant shooting star burst apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A shooting or falling star is the popular name for a meteor burning up in the atmosphere.

clue.text: Short story being broadcast — it could be gripping!

indicators.note: a short word has lost its tail, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a story is a tale
a programme being broadcast is on, on air

explanation.surface: A short story aired on radio might be gripping listening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gripping' suggests a thrilling story, but it is a claw literally gripping prey.
explanation.definitionFit: A talon is a bird of prey's claw, something that literally grips.

clue.text: Elegantly simple opener from Hitchin Town

parts.note: neat can mean elegantly simple, as in a neat design

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter, here taken from Hitchin

explanation.surface: A plain, stylish goal opens the scoring for Hitchin Town football club.
explanation.walkthrough: Hitchin Town is a real English football club, so 'Town' seems part of a name. NEATH is a town in south Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Neath is a market town in south Wales, an example of a town.

clue.text: Island in unsettled US area, or continental one?

indicators.note: the island letter is placed inside the scrambled letters
unsettled letters are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: An island sits in some unsettled region of the US, or perhaps of another continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unsettled' rearranges USAREA to EURASA, and I goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Eurasia is the combined landmass of Europe and Asia, so a continent of sorts.

clue.text: Sneaky-sounding attempt to see Irish county

indicators.note: something sounding like these words is said aloud and heard as another word

parts.note: sneaky means sly, a word heard here and written another way
an attempt is a go

explanation.surface: A furtive attempt is made to see a county in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Sligo is a county in the north-west of the Republic of Ireland, on the Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Musical drama extremely tiresome work

parts.note: an opera is a musical drama

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters, taken from tiresome

explanation.surface: An opera proves extremely tedious work to sit through.
explanation.definitionFit: To work, as a machine does, is to operate or function.

clue.text: Love trapped by one obscure colloquialism

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: the love letter is caught inside the obscure word

parts.note: dim means obscure or faint
love is nil in tennis, so O

explanation.surface: Love is caught up in an obscure expression.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is an expression peculiar to a language, much like a colloquialism.

clue.text: Poor place the owner soon abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned letters are left loose to be rearranged freely

explanation.surface: The owner quickly deserted a run-down property.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-horse town is a small, backward, poorly provided settlement.
